blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Daniel had served in Babylon a long, long time. King Darius thought so much of him that he planned to set him over the whole kingdom. And you know how that goes. The other leaders got jealous. They went looking for something wrong with him, and they could not find a thing. He was faithful. He was honest.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: So they figured the only way to catch Daniel was through his God. They talked the king into signing a law. Thirty days, nobody could pray to any god or any man but the king. Anybody who did would go to the lions.

verses.text: Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Look at what he did, Church. He did not hide. He did not change his schedule. He went home, opened his windows toward Jerusalem, got down on his knees, and prayed like he always had. A church mother I knew used to say, baby, you cannot start praying in the storm if you never prayed in the sunshine. Daniel had prayed in the sunshine.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The men found him praying and ran to the king. The king was sick about it, because he loved Daniel. He worked till the sun went down to find a way out. But a law of the Medes and Persians could not be changed.

verses.text: Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the den of lions. Now the king spake and said unto Daniel, Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the den of lions. Now the king spake and said unto Daniel,

segments.speaker: king
segments.text: Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Even the king who signed that order was hoping in Daniel's God. They rolled a stone over the mouth of the den and sealed it with the king's own ring. Then the king went home to his palace. No supper. No music. No sleep.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Think about that. The man in the lions' den had more peace than the man in the palace.

verses.text: Then the king arose very early in the morning, and went in haste unto the den of lions.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the king arose very early in the morning, and went in haste unto the den of lions.

verses.text: And when he came to the den, he cried with a lamentable voice unto Daniel: and the king spake and said to Daniel, O Daniel, servant of the living God, is thy God, whom thou servest continually, able to deliver thee from the lions?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when he came to the den, he cried with a lamentable voice unto Daniel: and the king spake and said to Daniel,

segments.speaker: king
segments.text: O Daniel, servant of the living God, is thy God, whom thou servest continually, able to deliver thee from the lions?

verses.text: Then said Daniel unto the king, O king, live for ever.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then said Daniel unto the king,

verses.text: My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.

verses.text: Then was the king exceeding glad for him, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then was the king exceeding glad for him, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The old spiritual asks it plain: didn't my Lord deliver Daniel? And the answer comes right back. He did. The story does not say the den was not real or that the lions were not hungry. It says God sent his angel and shut their mouths, and Daniel trusted his God. Somebody is praying with the windows open tonight. Keep on praying.
